azure_automation_openapi_dsc_configurati: `azure_automation_openapi_dsc_configuration` defines a PowerShell Desired State Configuration script managed by Azure Automation State Configuration, describing the target state for registered node(s).
azure_automation_openapi_dsc_node_config: `azure_automation_openapi_dsc_node_configuration` is a compiled DSC configuration assigned to specific registered node(s), the actual configuration those nodes are enforced against.
azure_automation_openapi_hybrid_runbook_: `azure_automation_openapi_hybrid_runbook_worker` registers a machine (on-premises or another cloud) as a hybrid worker, letting Azure Automation runbooks execute directly on it rather than Azure-hosted sandboxes.
`azure_automation_openapi_hybrid_runbook_worker_group` groups related hybrid runbook worker(s) together, that a runbook job can be targeted to run on any member of.
azure_automation_openapi_job: `azure_automation_openapi_job` is a single execution of an Azure Automation runbook.
azure_automation_openapi_job_schedule: `azure_automation_openapi_job_schedule` links an Azure Automation runbook to a schedule, triggering it to run automatically at the schedule's own defined times.
azure_automation_openapi_module: `azure_automation_openapi_module` imports a PowerShell module into an Azure Automation account, making its own cmdlets available to runbook(s).
azure_automation_openapi_package: `azure_automation_openapi_package` imports a Python package into an Azure Automation account, making it available to Python runbook(s).
azure_automation_openapi_private_endpoin: `azure_automation_openapi_private_endpoint_connection` represents the connection between a Private Endpoint and an Azure Automation account, tracking its own approval state.
azure_automation_openapi_runbook: `azure_automation_openapi_runbook` is the executable script (PowerShell, Python, or a graphical workflow) that Azure Automation runs, either on a schedule, on demand, or via webhook.
azure_automation_openapi_runtime_environ: `azure_automation_openapi_runtime_environment` defines a custom language version and package set that PowerShell or Python runbook(s) execute within, beyond Azure Automation's own default runtime.
azure_automation_openapi_schedule: `azure_automation_openapi_schedule` defines a recurring or one-time trigger time that Azure Automation runbook(s) can be linked to for automatic execution.
azure_automation_openapi_software_update: `azure_automation_openapi_software_update_configuration` schedules Azure Automation Update Management to deploy OS patches across a defined set of machine(s) on a recurring maintenance window.
azure_automation_openapi_source_control: `azure_automation_openapi_source_control` links an Azure Automation account to an external Git repository, syncing runbook source code automatically on push.
azure_automation_openapi_source_control_: `azure_automation_openapi_source_control_sync_job_by_id` starts a source control sync job, pulling the latest runbook source code from an Azure Automation account's own linked Git repository on demand.
azure_automation_openapi_variable: `azure_automation_openapi_variable` stores a named configuration value (plain or encrypted) within an Azure Automation account, referenced by runbook(s).
azure_automation_openapi_watcher: `azure_automation_openapi_watcher` runs a long-lived Azure Automation script that watches for a defined condition and triggers a follow-up runbook when it's detected.
azure_automation_openapi_webhook: `azure_automation_openapi_webhook` exposes an HTTP endpoint that, when called, triggers a specific Azure Automation runbook to run.
azure_availability_set: `azure_availability_set` groups VMs so a single hardware failure or maintenance event can't take down every instance of an application at once. Azure spreads the VMs across up to 3 fault domains (shared power and network switch) and up to 20 update domains (VMs that restart together during planned maintenance), and neither count can change after the set is created. There's no extra cost for using one, but Microsoft's own current guidance recommends Virtual Machine Scale Sets with flexible orchestration for new deployments needing the widest range of availability features.
azure_azureactivedirectory_privateendpoi: `azure_azureactivedirectory_privateendpointconnections_private_endpoint_connection` represents the connection between a Private Endpoint and Microsoft Entra ID's own Private Link resource, tracking its own approval state.
azure_azureactivedirectory_privatelinkfo: `azure_azureactivedirectory_privatelinkforazuread_private_link_policy` restricts Microsoft Entra ID sign-in for a tenant to only occur through an approved Private Link connection, blocking access from outside the configured network(s).
azure_azurestackhci_galleryimages_galler: `azure_azurestackhci_galleryimages_gallery_images` registers a VM gallery image (an OS image) available for provisioning new VM(s) on an Azure Stack HCI cluster.
azure_azurestackhci_hci_arc_setting: `azure_azurestackhci_hci_arc_setting` configures Azure Arc integration for an Azure Stack HCI cluster, enabling Arc extensions and hybrid management once registered.
azure_azurestackhci_hci_cluster: `azure_azurestackhci_hci_cluster` represents an Azure Stack HCI cluster's own Azure resource, the Arc-registered projection of the on-premises hyperconverged cluster.
azure_azurestackhci_hci_deployment_setti: `azure_azurestackhci_hci_deployment_setting` defines the full deployment configuration (networking, storage, node topology) an Azure Stack HCI cluster is initially deployed with.
azure_azurestackhci_hci_edge_device: `azure_azurestackhci_hci_edge_device` represents a single physical node's own Azure resource within an Azure Stack HCI deployment, prior to or during cluster formation.
azure_azurestackhci_hci_edge_device_job: `azure_azurestackhci_hci_edge_device_job` tracks an asynchronous operation (e.g. a firmware update) running against an Azure Stack HCI edge device.
azure_azurestackhci_hci_extension: `azure_azurestackhci_hci_extension` installs an Azure Arc extension onto an Azure Stack HCI cluster's own node(s), e.g. for monitoring or Kubernetes.
azure_azurestackhci_hci_security_setting: `azure_azurestackhci_hci_security_setting` reports and configures security posture settings (e.g. WDAC, Secured-core) for an Azure Stack HCI cluster.
azure_azurestackhci_hci_update: `azure_azurestackhci_hci_update` represents an available or applied software update for an Azure Stack HCI cluster.
azure_azurestackhci_hci_update_run: `azure_azurestackhci_hci_update_run` is a single execution of applying an update to an Azure Stack HCI cluster, tracked step by step.
azure_azurestackhci_logicalnetworks_logi: `azure_azurestackhci_logicalnetworks_logical_networks` defines a logical network on Azure Arc-enabled Azure Stack HCI, that VM(s) provisioned through Azure tooling are attached to.
azure_azurestackhci_marketplacegalleryim: `azure_azurestackhci_marketplacegalleryimages_marketplace_gallery_images` downloads a published Azure Marketplace VM image for use provisioning new VM(s) on an Azure Stack HCI cluster.
azure_azurestackhci_networkinterfaces_ne: `azure_azurestackhci_networkinterfaces_network_interfaces` is a virtual network interface attached to a VM running on Azure Arc-enabled Azure Stack HCI.
azure_azurestackhci_storagecontainers_st: `azure_azurestackhci_storagecontainers_storage_containers` defines a storage location on an Azure Stack HCI cluster that VM disk(s) provisioned through Azure tooling are placed in.
azure_azurestackhci_virtualharddisks_vir: `azure_azurestackhci_virtualharddisks_virtual_hard_disks` is a virtual hard disk attached to a VM running on Azure Arc-enabled Azure Stack HCI.
azure_batch_openapi_application: `azure_batch_openapi_application` registers a versioned application package with an Azure Batch account, deployable to compute node(s) for task execution.
azure_batch_openapi_application_package: `azure_batch_openapi_application_package` is a specific uploaded version of an Azure Batch application, containing the actual executable and supporting file(s).
azure_batch_openapi_batch_account: `azure_batch_openapi_batch_account` is the top-level Azure Batch resource that pool(s), job(s), and application(s) are created within, for large-scale parallel and HPC batch job execution.
azure_batch_openapi_pool: `azure_batch_openapi_pool` is a collection of compute node(s) within an Azure Batch account that job(s) and their own task(s) actually run on.
azure_billing_openapi_associated_tenant: `azure_billing_openapi_associated_tenant` links an additional Microsoft Entra ID tenant to a billing account, letting resources in that tenant be billed against the account.
azure_billing_openapi_billing_account: `azure_billing_openapi_billing_account` is the top-level Microsoft Cost Management + Billing resource representing a billing relationship with Microsoft, that billing profile(s) and invoice(s) are organized under.
azure_billing_openapi_billing_profile: `azure_billing_openapi_billing_profile` defines a set of invoice(s) and payment method within a billing account, e.g. for billing a specific department or project separately.
azure_billing_openapi_billing_request: `azure_billing_openapi_billing_request` is a pending request to grant access to a billing account, profile, or invoice section, requiring approval before it takes effect.
azure_billing_openapi_billing_role_assig: `azure_billing_openapi_billing_role_assignment` grants a principal a specific billing role (e.g. Owner, Contributor, Reader) scoped to a billing account, profile, or invoice section.
azure_billing_openapi_billing_subscripti: `azure_billing_openapi_billing_subscription` is the billing-side record of an Azure subscription, tracking which invoice section it's billed under and its own product/plan.
`azure_billing_openapi_billing_subscription_alias` creates a new Azure subscription (or renames/moves an existing one between billing scopes) via the billing subscription alias API.
azure_billing_openapi_customer_policy: `azure_billing_openapi_customer_policy` configures policy setting(s) (e.g. whether the customer can view charges) that a CSP partner applies to a customer's own billing account.
azure_billing_openapi_invoice_section: `azure_billing_openapi_invoice_section` further subdivides a billing profile's own single invoice into separate section(s), e.g. for cost tracking per team without needing separate invoices.
azure_billing_openapi_partner_transfer_d: `azure_billing_openapi_partner_transfer_details` tracks a CSP partner-initiated request to transfer billing ownership of subscription(s) to a different partner or customer.
azure_billing_openapi_product: `azure_billing_openapi_product` is a purchased Azure offer (e.g. a reservation or a software plan) billed under a billing account, tracked independently of the subscription it's associated with.
azure_billing_openapi_recipient_transfer: `azure_billing_openapi_recipient_transfer_details` tracks the recipient side of a billing ownership transfer request for Azure subscription(s), letting the recipient accept or decline.
azure_billing_openapi_transfer_details: `azure_billing_openapi_transfer_details` records a request to transfer billing ownership of Azure subscription(s), product(s), or reservation(s) to a different billing account.
azure_botservice_bot: `azure_botservice_bot` registers a conversational bot with Azure AI Bot Service, the resource its own channel(s) and connection(s) are configured under.
azure_botservice_bot_channel: `azure_botservice_bot_channel` connects an Azure AI Bot Service bot to a specific messaging channel (Teams, Slack, web chat), making it reachable from that platform.
azure_botservice_connection_setting: `azure_botservice_connection_setting` stores OAuth connection settings an Azure AI Bot Service bot uses to authenticate to an external service on behalf of a user.
azure_botservice_private_endpoint_connec: `azure_botservice_private_endpoint_connection` represents the connection between a Private Endpoint and an Azure AI Bot Service bot, tracking its own approval state.
azure_capacity_reservation: `azure_capacity_reservation` reserves compute capacity for one specific VM size in one region or zone, for as long as you keep it. Unlike a Reserved Instance, there's no one- or three-year term: you create and delete a reservation whenever you want, and it's billed at the same pay-as-you-go rate as the VM size itself whether a VM is actually using it or not. A VM only consumes the reservation if it explicitly specifies it in its own properties.
azure_capacity_reservation_group: `azure_capacity_reservation_group` is the parent resource every individual capacity reservation belongs to. It pins the region (and, optionally, which availability zones are eligible) for every reservation created inside it, and it's what a VM's own properties reference to actually consume a reservation -- a group can hold at most one reservation per VM size per zone.
azure_cdn_openapi_afddomain: `azure_cdn_openapi_afddomain` maps a custom domain to an Azure Front Door endpoint, the current-generation (AFD Standard/Premium) equivalent of a classic CDN custom domain.
azure_cdn_openapi_afdendpoint: `azure_cdn_openapi_afdendpoint` is the entry point through which Azure Front Door serves traffic for one or more custom domain(s), routed to origin group(s) via defined route(s).
azure_cdn_openapi_afdorigin: `azure_cdn_openapi_afdorigin` defines a single backend server Azure Front Door retrieves content from, within an origin group.
azure_cdn_openapi_afdorigin_group: `azure_cdn_openapi_afdorigin_group` groups related origin(s) together in Azure Front Door, providing health-probe-based load balancing and failover across them.
azure_cdn_openapi_cdn_web_application_fi: `azure_cdn_openapi_cdn_web_application_firewall_policy` defines the Web Application Firewall rule(s) (managed or custom) applied to matching requests reaching an Azure Front Door or CDN endpoint.
azure_cdn_openapi_custom_domain: `azure_cdn_openapi_custom_domain` maps a custom domain to a classic Azure CDN endpoint.
azure_cdn_openapi_endpoint: `azure_cdn_openapi_endpoint` is the entry point serving cached content for a classic Azure CDN profile, forwarding uncached requests to its own configured origin.
azure_cdn_openapi_origin: `azure_cdn_openapi_origin` defines the backend server a classic Azure CDN endpoint retrieves and caches content from.
azure_cdn_openapi_origin_group: `azure_cdn_openapi_origin_group` groups related origin(s) together in a classic Azure CDN profile, providing failover across them.
azure_cdn_openapi_profile: `azure_cdn_openapi_profile` is the top-level Azure CDN or Front Door resource that endpoint(s), origin group(s), and their own configuration are created within.
azure_cdn_openapi_route: `azure_cdn_openapi_route` maps an incoming Azure Front Door request pattern (domain and path) to a specific origin group, with its own caching and protocol behavior.
azure_cdn_openapi_rule: `azure_cdn_openapi_rule` defines a match condition and action(s) (e.g. a redirect or header modification) applied to matching requests within an Azure Front Door or CDN rule set.
azure_cdn_openapi_rule_set: `azure_cdn_openapi_rule_set` groups related rule(s) together, applied to route(s) referencing the rule set within Azure Front Door or CDN.
azure_cdn_openapi_secret: `azure_cdn_openapi_secret` stores a TLS certificate or managed identity credential used by Azure Front Door for custom domain HTTPS or origin authentication.
azure_cdn_openapi_security_policy: `azure_cdn_openapi_security_policy` attaches a Web Application Firewall policy to specific domain(s) served by an Azure Front Door profile.
azure_chaos_openapi_capability: `azure_chaos_openapi_capability` enables a specific fault-injection action type (e.g. a network latency or CPU pressure fault) on an Azure Chaos Studio target.
azure_chaos_openapi_experiment: `azure_chaos_openapi_experiment` defines an Azure Chaos Studio experiment -- an ordered sequence of fault-injection step(s) run against target resource(s) to test their own resilience.
azure_chaos_openapi_target: `azure_chaos_openapi_target` onboards a resource to Azure Chaos Studio, enabling fault-injection capability(ies) to be run against it.
azure_codesigning_codesigningaccount_cer: `azure_codesigning_codesigningaccount_certificate_profile` defines a certificate profile (a specific signing identity and validity policy) within a Trusted Signing account, that signing request(s) are issued against.
azure_codesigning_codesigningaccount_cod: `azure_codesigning_codesigningaccount_code_signing_account` is a Trusted Signing account, providing managed code-signing certificates without the caller having to procure and rotate them manually.
azure_cognitiveservices_account: `azure_cognitiveservices_account` provisions an Azure AI services (Cognitive Services) account -- or an Azure AI Foundry (Microsoft Foundry) resource -- the top-level container that model deployment(s) and API access are billed and managed under.
azure_cognitiveservices_agent_applicatio: `azure_cognitiveservices_agent_application` registers an AI agent application built on Azure AI Foundry's own Agent Service, the deployable unit an agent's tools and instructions are packaged into.
azure_cognitiveservices_agent_deployment: `azure_cognitiveservices_agent_deployment` is a specific, running deployment of an Azure AI Foundry agent application, servable for real conversation traffic.
azure_cognitiveservices_capability_host: `azure_cognitiveservices_capability_host` provisions the compute and storage backing a specific AI capability (e.g. agent execution) within an Azure AI Foundry account.
azure_cognitiveservices_commitment_plan: `azure_cognitiveservices_commitment_plan` purchases a fixed monthly commitment tier for an Azure AI services feature (e.g. Translator or Speech), at a discount versus pay-as-you-go pricing.
azure_cognitiveservices_commitment_plan_: `azure_cognitiveservices_commitment_plan_account_association` attaches an Azure AI services account to a commitment plan, applying the plan's own discounted pricing to that account's usage.
azure_cognitiveservices_connection_prope: `azure_cognitiveservices_connection_properties_v2_basic_resource` defines a connection from an Azure AI Foundry account to an external resource (a data source, an API key-authenticated service).
azure_cognitiveservices_defender_for_ais: `azure_cognitiveservices_defender_for_aisetting` enables Microsoft Defender for AI protection on an Azure AI services account, surfacing threat alerts for anomalous or malicious AI workload activity in Microsoft Defender for Cloud.
azure_cognitiveservices_deployment: `azure_cognitiveservices_deployment` is a specific model deployment (e.g. a GPT or embedding model) on an Azure AI services / Azure OpenAI account, servable for inference calls.
azure_cognitiveservices_encryption_scope: `azure_cognitiveservices_encryption_scope` defines a customer-managed encryption key configuration scoped to a subset of data within an Azure AI services account.
azure_cognitiveservices_managed_network_: `azure_cognitiveservices_managed_network_settings_properties_basic_resource` configures whether an Azure AI Foundry account's own managed virtual network allows all outbound traffic by default or only explicitly approved outbound rule(s).
azure_cognitiveservices_network_security: `azure_cognitiveservices_network_security_perimeter_configuration` associates an Azure AI services account with a network security perimeter, restricting its own network access to the perimeter's own boundary rules.
azure_cognitiveservices_outbound_rule_ba: `azure_cognitiveservices_outbound_rule_basic_resource` defines an allowed outbound network destination for an Azure AI Foundry account's own managed virtual network, permitting egress to a specific service.
azure_cognitiveservices_private_endpoint: `azure_cognitiveservices_private_endpoint_connection` represents the connection between a Private Endpoint and an Azure AI services account, tracking its own approval state.
azure_cognitiveservices_project: `azure_cognitiveservices_project` is a project within an Azure AI Foundry account, scoping model deployment(s), agent(s), and connection(s) to a specific team or workload.
azure_cognitiveservices_project_capabili: `azure_cognitiveservices_project_capability_host` provisions the compute and storage backing a specific AI capability (e.g. agent execution) scoped to a single Azure AI Foundry project, rather than the whole account.
azure_cognitiveservices_quota_tier: `azure_cognitiveservices_quota_tier` reports the throughput quota tier assigned to a specific model within an Azure AI services account, e.g. tokens-per-minute limits.
azure_cognitiveservices_rai_blocklist: `azure_cognitiveservices_rai_blocklist` defines a custom list of blocked term(s) or phrase(s) enforced by a Responsible AI content filter policy on Azure AI services model deployment(s).
azure_cognitiveservices_rai_blocklist_it: `azure_cognitiveservices_rai_blocklist_item` is a single blocked term or phrase within a Responsible AI blocklist.
azure_cognitiveservices_rai_external_saf: `azure_cognitiveservices_rai_external_safety_provider_schema` integrates a third-party content-safety guardrail provider (e.g. Palo Alto Networks) into an Azure AI Foundry Responsible AI policy, alongside Microsoft's own built-in filters.
azure_cognitiveservices_rai_policy: `azure_cognitiveservices_rai_policy` defines the Responsible AI content filter configuration (categories, severity thresholds) enforced on Azure AI services model deployment(s) it's attached to.
azure_cognitiveservices_rai_tool_label: `azure_cognitiveservices_rai_tool_label` classifies a specific tool an AI agent can call under a Responsible AI risk category, so Foundry Guardrails can apply appropriate policy when that tool is invoked.
azure_cognitiveservices_rai_topic: `azure_cognitiveservices_rai_topic` defines a custom sensitive topic a Responsible AI content filter policy detects and restricts, beyond Microsoft's own built-in harm categories.
azure_communication_openapi_communicatio: `azure_communication_openapi_communication_service_resource` is an Azure Communication Services resource, the top-level container that chat, voice, video, SMS, and email capability(ies) are provisioned under.
azure_communication_openapi_domain_resou: `azure_communication_openapi_domain_resource` registers a sending domain (Azure-managed or a caller-verified custom domain) for Azure Communication Services Email.
azure_communication_openapi_email_servic: `azure_communication_openapi_email_service_resource` is an Email Communication Services resource, that domain(s) used to send email through Azure Communication Services are registered under.
azure_communication_openapi_sender_usern: `azure_communication_openapi_sender_username_resource` defines a sender username (the part before `@`) permitted to send email from a verified domain in Azure Communication Services.
azure_communication_openapi_smtp_usernam: `azure_communication_openapi_smtp_username_resource` is a SMTP-specific credential username for authenticating to Azure Communication Services Email over SMTP.
azure_communication_openapi_suppression_: `azure_communication_openapi_suppression_list_address_resource` is a single email address added to an Azure Communication Services suppression list, blocking further email delivery to it.

`azure_communication_openapi_suppression_list_resource` is a named list of email address(es) Azure Communication Services Email excludes from delivery, e.g. addresses that previously bounced or unsubscribed.
azure_compute_containerservice_container: `azure_compute_containerservice_container_service` is the legacy Azure Container Service (ACS) resource, an early, now largely superseded orchestrator deployment predating Azure Kubernetes Service.
azure_confidentialledger_openapi_confide: `azure_confidentialledger_openapi_confidential_ledger` is a Confidential Ledger instance, a tamper-proof, cryptographically verifiable data store running inside secure hardware enclaves.
azure_consumption_openapi_budget: `azure_consumption_openapi_budget` sets a spending threshold on a scope and triggers notification(s) when actual or forecasted spend crosses it, via the Consumption API's own budget resource.
azure_containerservice_fleets_auto_upgra: `azure_containerservice_fleets_auto_upgrade_profile` schedules AKS Fleet member cluster(s) to be automatically upgraded to a new Kubernetes or node image version on a defined cadence.
azure_containerservice_fleets_fleet: `azure_containerservice_fleets_fleet` is the top-level AKS Fleet Manager resource, coordinating Kubernetes version upgrades and workload placement across multiple member AKS cluster(s).
azure_containerservice_fleets_fleet_mana: `azure_containerservice_fleets_fleet_managed_namespace` provisions the same managed Kubernetes namespace configuration across every member cluster of an AKS Fleet.
azure_containerservice_fleets_fleet_memb: `azure_containerservice_fleets_fleet_member` joins an existing AKS cluster to a Fleet, making it eligible for Fleet-orchestrated update runs and multi-cluster workload placement.
azure_containerservice_fleets_fleet_upda: `azure_containerservice_fleets_fleet_update_strategy` defines a reusable, ordered stage sequence for rolling an update across an AKS Fleet's own member cluster(s), that update run(s) can reference.
azure_containerservice_fleets_update_run: `azure_containerservice_fleets_update_run` is a single execution of rolling a Kubernetes or node image update across an AKS Fleet's own member cluster(s), following a defined update strategy.
azure_containerservice_managedclusters_a: `azure_containerservice_managedclusters_agent_pool` is a group of node(s) with shared configuration (VM size, scaling, taints) within an AKS cluster.
azure_containerservice_managedclusters_i: `azure_containerservice_managedclusters_identity_binding` (preview) lets multiple AKS clusters share a single user-assigned managed identity's own federated identity credential for workload identity, working around the per-identity FIC quota that limited large-scale multi-cluster deployments.
azure_containerservice_managedclusters_m: `azure_containerservice_managedclusters_maintenance_configuration` defines a preferred maintenance window for control plane and node OS updates on an AKS cluster.
`azure_containerservice_managedclusters_managed_cluster` is an Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) cluster, the managed Kubernetes control plane and node infrastructure that workload(s) are deployed to.

`azure_containerservice_managedclusters_managed_namespace` provisions a Kubernetes namespace on an AKS cluster as its own manageable Azure resource, with per-namespace resource quotas, network policy, and labels applied declaratively.
azure_containerservice_managedclusters_p: `azure_containerservice_managedclusters_private_endpoint_connection` represents the connection between a Private Endpoint and an AKS cluster's own private API server, tracking its own approval state.
azure_containerservice_managedclusters_r: `azure_containerservice_managedclusters_run_command_result` reports the output of a command run against a private AKS cluster's own API server via the Run Command feature, without needing direct network access to it.
azure_containerservice_managedclusters_s: `azure_containerservice_managedclusters_snapshot` captures a point-in-time configuration snapshot of an AKS cluster or node pool, usable as a template for creating new ones with the same settings.
azure_containerservice_managedclusters_t: `azure_containerservice_managedclusters_trusted_access_role_binding` grants another Azure resource's own system-assigned managed identity secure, RBAC-scoped access to an AKS cluster's own API server, without exposing the cluster to public networks.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_cassandra_keyspa: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_cassandra_keyspace_get_results` is a Cassandra API keyspace within a Cosmos DB account, the container tables in that API surface are organized under.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_cassandra_role_a: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_cassandra_role_assignment_resource` grants a Cassandra API role definition's own permissions to a specific identity within a Cosmos DB account.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_cassandra_role_d: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_cassandra_role_definition_resource` defines a set of data-plane permissions that can be granted to identities accessing a Cosmos DB account through its Cassandra API.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_cassandra_table_: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_cassandra_table_get_results` is a table within a Cosmos DB account's Cassandra API keyspace.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_client_encryptio: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_client_encryption_key_get_results` is a client-side encryption key registered with a Cosmos DB database, used to encrypt specific field(s) before they're sent to the service.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_cluster_resource: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_cluster_resource` provisions an Azure Managed Instance for Apache Cassandra cluster, a fully managed deployment of open-source Cassandra.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_data_center_reso: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_data_center_resource` is a single data center (a group of nodes in one region) within an Azure Managed Instance for Apache Cassandra cluster.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_database_account: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_database_account_get_results` is a Cosmos DB account, the top-level resource that database(s) across any of its enabled API surfaces (SQL, MongoDB, Cassandra, Gremlin, Table) are created within.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_fleet_resource: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_fleet_resource` is a Cosmos DB Fleet, a top-level resource organizing and managing multiple Cosmos DB account(s) -- typically one per tenant -- across subscriptions and resource groups for a single multitenant application.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_fleetspace_accou: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_fleetspace_account_resource` associates a specific Cosmos DB account with a fleetspace, making it part of that fleetspace's own shared throughput pool.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_fleetspace_resou: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_fleetspace_resource` is a logical grouping of Cosmos DB account(s) within a fleet, optionally sharing a pooled throughput allocation across every account in the group.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_gremlin_database: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_gremlin_database_get_results` is a database within a Cosmos DB account's Gremlin (graph) API surface, the container graph(s) are organized under.
azure_cosmos_db_openapi_gremlin_graph_ge: `azure_cosmos_db_openapi_gremlin_graph_get_results` is a graph within a Cosmos DB account's Gremlin API database, storing vertex and edge data queried via the Gremlin traversal language.

azure_databox_job_resource: `azure_databox_job_resource` orders a physical Azure Data Box appliance shipped to a customer site for bulk offline data transfer into or out of Azure.
azure_databricks_openapi_access_connecto: `azure_databricks_openapi_access_connector` is a managed identity resource letting an Azure Databricks workspace securely access other Azure resource(s) (e.g. a storage account) using Azure AD authentication, without embedding credentials.

azure_datafactory_openapi_dataset_resour: `azure_datafactory_openapi_dataset_resource` defines a named reference to data (a table, file, or folder) at a specific linked service, that pipeline activities read from or write to.

azure_datafactory_openapi_pipeline_resou: `azure_datafactory_openapi_pipeline_resource` defines an ordered sequence of activity(ies) (copy, transform, control-flow) within a Data Factory, the unit that's actually triggered and run.
azure_datafactory_openapi_private_endpoi: `azure_datafactory_openapi_private_endpoint_connection_resource` represents the connection between a Private Endpoint and a Data Factory, tracking its own approval state.
azure_datafactory_openapi_trigger_resour: `azure_datafactory_openapi_trigger_resource` defines when a Data Factory pipeline runs automatically -- on a schedule, in response to a storage event, or when a tumbling window elapses.
azure_datamigration_sqlmigration_databas: `azure_datamigration_sqlmigration_database_migration_cosmos_db_mongo` tracks a single database migration into Cosmos DB for MongoDB through Azure Database Migration Service.

azure_dataprotection_operation_job_exten: `azure_dataprotection_operation_job_extended_info` reports the current progress and extended status detail of a long-running Data Protection async operation.
azure_dataprotection_resource_guard_prox: `azure_dataprotection_resource_guard_proxy_base_resource` links a Backup vault to a Resource Guard, enforcing multi-user authorization (MUA) on that vault's own critical operations -- disabling immutability, changing retention, or deleting backups all then require a second approver who doesn't control the vault.

azure_dedicated_host: `azure_dedicated_host` maps to one physical server in an Azure datacenter, allocated entirely to your own subscription -- no other customer's VMs are ever placed on it. Beyond the isolation itself, a dedicated host gives you Azure Hybrid Benefit licensing, control over when platform maintenance actually lands on your hardware, and a say in which of your own workloads share the same physical memory and storage. Each host is created inside a host group and can run multiple VMs at once, as long as they're all from the same size series.
azure_dedicated_host_group: `azure_dedicated_host_group` is the resource that represents a collection of dedicated hosts. The group also controls whether new VMs get placed onto its hosts automatically or only when you explicitly pick a host.

azure_devtestlabs_dtl_lab_cost: `azure_devtestlabs_dtl_lab_cost` reports the lab's own accumulated and projected spend, broken down by resource, for a specified time period.
azure_devtestlabs_dtl_lab_virtual_machin: `azure_devtestlabs_dtl_lab_virtual_machine` is a virtual machine created within a DevTest Lab, distinct from a plain Azure VM in that it's subject to the lab's own cost, schedule, and access policies.
azure_devtestlabs_dtl_notification_chann: `azure_devtestlabs_dtl_notification_channel` configures where a lab sends event notifications (e.g. an autoshutdown warning), such as a webhook URL or email address.
azure_devtestlabs_dtl_policy: `azure_devtestlabs_dtl_policy` is a lab policy -- a constraint like a maximum VM count per user or an allowed VM size list -- enforced against every virtual machine created in the lab.
azure_devtestlabs_dtl_schedule: `azure_devtestlabs_dtl_schedule` is an automated schedule within a lab, most commonly an auto-shutdown or auto-start time applied to a lab virtual machine or the whole lab.

azure_netapp_volume_group_details: `azure_netapp_volume_group_details` groups related Azure NetApp Files volume(s) together (e.g. for a SAP HANA deployment), provisioned and managed as a coordinated set.
azure_netapp_volume_quota_rule: `azure_netapp_volume_quota_rule` sets a per-user or per-group storage quota on an Azure NetApp Files volume.
azure_network_applicationgateway_applica: `azure_network_applicationgateway_application_gateway` is an Azure Application Gateway, a regional Layer 7 load balancer with integrated Web Application Firewall support.

azure_network_applicationgateway_web_app: `azure_network_applicationgateway_web_application_firewall_policy` defines the Web Application Firewall rule(s) (managed or custom) applied to matching requests reaching an Application Gateway.
azure_network_expressroute_express_route: `azure_network_expressroute_express_route_circuit` is the logical connection to a connectivity provider's own ExpressRoute service, that private and Microsoft peering(s) are established over.
`azure_network_expressroute_express_route_circuit_authorization` generates an authorization key letting another subscription's own virtual network gateway connect to this ExpressRoute circuit.

`azure_network_expressroute_express_route_circuit_connection` connects two ExpressRoute circuits directly together, e.g. to link a customer's own on-premises networks across different peering locations.
`azure_network_expressroute_express_route_circuit_peering` configures a specific peering type (Azure Private or Microsoft) on an ExpressRoute circuit, including its own BGP session details.

`azure_network_expressroute_express_route_cross_connection` is the connectivity provider-managed representation of a customer's own ExpressRoute circuit, used by providers to configure circuit-level settings on the customer's behalf.
`azure_network_expressroute_express_route_cross_connection_peering` configures a peering on an ExpressRoute cross connection, the provider-side counterpart to a circuit peering.
`azure_network_expressroute_express_route_lag` groups multiple ExpressRoute Direct physical port(s) together as a single logical link, for combined bandwidth and redundancy.
`azure_network_expressroute_express_route_port` provisions a dedicated, physical ExpressRoute Direct port pair at a Microsoft peering location, that circuit(s) can be created directly on top of.

azure_network_expressroute_route_filter: `azure_network_expressroute_route_filter` restricts which BGP community-tagged route(s) are advertised over an ExpressRoute circuit's own Microsoft Peering, limiting the Microsoft service(s) reachable through it.
azure_network_expressroute_route_filter_: `azure_network_expressroute_route_filter_rule` is a single BGP community match rule within an ExpressRoute route filter.
azure_network_expressroute_service_endpo: `azure_network_expressroute_service_endpoint_policy` restricts which specific Azure service resource(s) a subnet's own VNet service endpoint traffic can reach.

azure_network_firewall_azure_firewall: `azure_network_firewall_azure_firewall` is an Azure Firewall instance, a managed, cloud-native network firewall providing stateful traffic filtering, threat intelligence, and TLS inspection for a virtual network or hub.
azure_network_firewallpolicy_firewall_po: `azure_network_firewallpolicy_firewall_policy` defines the rule collection(s), threat intelligence, and TLS inspection settings applied by one or more Azure Firewall instance(s).

azure_network_firstpartyservicetag_first: `azure_network_firstpartyservicetag_first_party_service_tag` reports a Microsoft first-party service's own IP address range grouping, usable in network security rules the same way a regular Azure service tag is.
azure_network_interconnectgroup_intercon: `azure_network_interconnectgroup_interconnect_group` groups ExpressRoute Direct port pair(s) together at the datacenter interconnection level, coordinating link status across the group.
azure_network_loadbalancer_backend_addre: `azure_network_loadbalancer_backend_address_pool` is the set of backend instance(s) or IP address(es) an Azure Load Balancer distributes matching traffic across.
azure_network_loadbalancer_inbound_nat_r: `azure_network_loadbalancer_inbound_nat_rule` forwards traffic on a specific frontend port of an Azure Load Balancer to one specific backend instance, e.g. for direct RDP/SSH access to an individual VM.
azure_network_loadbalancer_load_balancer: `azure_network_loadbalancer_load_balancer` is an Azure Load Balancer, distributing inbound Layer 4 traffic across a pool of backend instance(s) based on load-balancing rule(s).
azure_network_networkgateway_local_netwo: `azure_network_networkgateway_local_network_gateway` represents an on-premises VPN endpoint's own public IP address and address space, referenced by a site-to-site VPN connection.
azure_network_networkgateway_virtual_net: `azure_network_networkgateway_virtual_network_gateway` provisions a VPN or ExpressRoute gateway for a virtual network, terminating site-to-site, point-to-site, or ExpressRoute connections into it.

azure_network_networkmanager_admin_rule_: `azure_network_networkmanager_admin_rule_collection` groups related security admin rule(s) together within an Azure Virtual Network Manager security admin configuration.
azure_network_networkmanager_base_admin_: `azure_network_networkmanager_base_admin_rule` is the base type for a security admin or default rule enforced centrally across a Virtual Network Manager network group, evaluated before any local NSG rules.
azure_network_networkmanager_commit: `azure_network_networkmanager_commit` deploys a Virtual Network Manager configuration (connectivity or security) to its own target scope, making it take actual effect.
azure_network_networkmanager_connectivit: `azure_network_networkmanager_connectivity_configuration` defines the connectivity topology (hub-and-spoke or mesh) Azure Virtual Network Manager establishes across the virtual network(s) in a network group.
azure_network_networkmanager_network_gro: `azure_network_networkmanager_network_group` is a named collection of virtual network(s), defined statically or dynamically via Azure Policy conditions, that Virtual Network Manager configurations are applied to.
azure_network_networkmanager_network_man: `azure_network_networkmanager_network_manager` is the top-level Azure Virtual Network Manager resource, centrally managing connectivity and security configuration across virtual network(s) within its own scope.

`azure_network_networkmanager_network_manager_routing_configuration` defines centralized routing rule(s) Virtual Network Manager applies across the virtual network(s) in a network group.
azure_network_networkmanager_routing_rul: `azure_network_networkmanager_routing_rule` is a single centrally managed route within a Virtual Network Manager routing configuration.
`azure_network_networkmanager_routing_rule_collection` groups related centrally managed routing rule(s) together within a Virtual Network Manager routing configuration.
azure_network_networkmanager_scope_conne: `azure_network_networkmanager_scope_connection` extends a Virtual Network Manager instance's own management scope to include another subscription or management group.
azure_network_networkmanager_security_ad: `azure_network_networkmanager_security_admin_configuration` defines centrally enforced security admin rule(s) that Virtual Network Manager applies across the virtual network(s) in a network group, taking precedence over local NSG rules.
azure_network_networkmanager_security_us: `azure_network_networkmanager_security_user_configuration` defines security user rule(s) Virtual Network Manager applies across the virtual network(s) in a network group, evaluated after local NSG rules.
`azure_network_networkmanager_security_user_rule` is a single centrally managed security rule within a Virtual Network Manager security user configuration.
`azure_network_networkmanager_security_user_rule_collection` groups related security user rule(s) together within a Virtual Network Manager security user configuration.
azure_network_networkmanager_static_memb: `azure_network_networkmanager_static_member` explicitly adds a specific virtual network to a Virtual Network Manager network group, as an alternative to dynamic, Azure Policy-based group membership.
azure_network_networksecurityperimeter_n: `azure_network_networksecurityperimeter_network_security_perimeter` is the top-level Network Security Perimeter resource, defining a logical boundary around a group of PaaS resource(s) that access is restricted to and from as a unit, regardless of their own individual network configuration.

`azure_network_networksecurityperimeter_nsp_logging_configuration` configures diagnostic logging of access rule evaluation decisions across a Network Security Perimeter.
`azure_network_networksecurityperimeter_nsp_profile` groups access rule(s) together within a Network Security Perimeter, that associated resource(s) inherit collectively.
azure_network_networkwatcher_connection_: `azure_network_networkwatcher_connection_analyzer` (Connection Troubleshoot) runs a one-off connectivity check between a source and destination, reporting whether the connection succeeds and the hop(s) it takes.

azure_network_networkwatcher_flow_log: `azure_network_networkwatcher_flow_log` records accepted and denied IP traffic flow information for a Network Security Group, written to a Storage account for traffic analytics and security auditing.
azure_network_networkwatcher_network_wat: `azure_network_networkwatcher_network_watcher` is the regional Network Watcher resource that diagnostic and monitoring tool(s) (flow logs, connection monitors, packet capture) are created under.
azure_network_networkwatcher_packet_capt: `azure_network_networkwatcher_packet_capture_result` captures raw network traffic to and from a specific VM, triggerable remotely without installing packet-capture software manually.
azure_network_servicegateway_service_gat: `azure_network_servicegateway_service_gateway` is a service gateway resource extending on-premises Active Directory-style connectivity or other managed gateway functionality into a virtual network.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_address_pre: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_address_prefix_set` defines a named, reusable set of IP address prefixes managed by Azure Virtual Network Manager, referenced by IP address management pools and connectivity/security configurations.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_application: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_application_security_group` groups network interface(s) together as a named, logical unit, letting network security group rules reference the group instead of raw IP addresses.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_bastion_hos: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_bastion_host` provisions Azure Bastion, a managed jump host providing secure RDP/SSH access to VMs over the Azure portal without exposing them to public IP addresses.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_custom_ip_p: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_custom_ip_prefix` brings a caller-owned public IP address range into Azure for advertisement and use, via Custom IP Prefix (BYOIP).
azure_network_virtualnetwork_ddos_custom: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_ddos_custom_policy` overrides Azure DDoS Protection's own default traffic thresholds for a specific public IP address, tuning detection sensitivity for that resource's own traffic pattern.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_ddos_protec: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_ddos_protection_plan` subscribes one or more virtual networks to Azure DDoS Network Protection, providing enhanced mitigation, telemetry, and cost protection beyond the free basic tier.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_inbound_sec: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_inbound_security_rule` allows specific inbound traffic through an Azure Firewall-integrated security partner provider before it reaches a virtual network.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_ip_allocati: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_ip_allocation` reserves a specific IP address block for a defined purpose (e.g. an Azure PaaS service delegation) within a virtual network's own address space.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_ip_group: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_ip_group` is a named, reusable collection of IP address(es) or address range(s) that Azure Firewall rules can reference by name instead of enumerating addresses inline.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_ipam_pool: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_ipam_pool` reserves a block of IP address space under Azure Virtual Network Manager's own IP Address Management capability, that virtual networks draw non-overlapping address ranges from automatically.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_nat_gateway: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_nat_gateway` provides managed, scalable outbound internet connectivity (source NAT) for resources in an attached subnet, without requiring a public IP directly on each resource.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_network_vir: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_network_virtual_appliance` deploys a third-party network virtual appliance (firewall, router) from the Azure Marketplace into a virtual hub, for traffic inspection and routing.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_private_dns: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_private_dns_zone_group` links a Private Endpoint to Private DNS zone(s), automatically creating and maintaining the DNS record(s) that resolve to the endpoint's private IP address.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_public_ippr: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_public_ipprefix` reserves a contiguous, statically allocated range of public IP addresses that individual public IP address resources can be created from.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_reachabilit: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_reachability_analysis_intent` defines the source and destination traffic path Azure Virtual Network Manager's own Network Verifier should evaluate for reachability, before any actual analysis run is executed.

azure_network_virtualnetwork_route: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_route` is a single custom route within a route table, directing traffic matching an address prefix to a specific next hop.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_security_pa: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_security_partner_provider` integrates a supported third-party security provider (e.g. Check Point, Zscaler) with an Azure Firewall-managed virtual hub for traffic inspection.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_security_ru: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_security_rule` is a single custom allow/deny rule within a network security group, evaluated in priority order against matching traffic.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_static_cidr: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_static_cidr` tracks an IP address range already in use outside Azure Virtual Network Manager's own control (e.g. on-premises or manually allocated) within an IPAM pool, preventing it from being allocated again.

azure_network_virtualnetwork_verifier_wo: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_verifier_workspace` is the top-level Azure Virtual Network Manager resource that reachability analysis intent(s) and their own analysis run(s) are created under.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_virtual_app: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_virtual_appliance_site` defines a branch site whose own address space is advertised to and routed through a network virtual appliance deployed in a virtual hub.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_virtual_net: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_virtual_network_peering` connects two virtual networks together at the network layer, letting resources in each communicate using private IP addresses as if they were on the same network.
azure_network_virtualnetwork_virtual_rou: `azure_network_virtualnetwork_virtual_router` provisions Azure Route Server, a managed BGP route reflector that lets network virtual appliances exchange dynamic routes directly with a virtual network without static route table configuration.

azure_network_virtualnetworkappliance_vi: `azure_network_virtualnetworkappliance_virtual_network_appliance` deploys a third-party network virtual appliance (firewall, router) from the Azure Marketplace directly into a virtual network.
azure_network_virtualwan_bgp_connection: `azure_network_virtualwan_bgp_connection` establishes a BGP peering session between a Virtual WAN hub and an external router, exchanging dynamic routes without static route configuration.
azure_network_virtualwan_connection_poli: `azure_network_virtualwan_connection_policy` restricts which point-to-site VPN group(s) or attribute(s) are permitted to establish a connection through a Virtual WAN P2S gateway.
azure_network_virtualwan_express_route_c: `azure_network_virtualwan_express_route_connection` connects an ExpressRoute circuit to a Virtual WAN hub's own ExpressRoute gateway.
azure_network_virtualwan_express_route_g: `azure_network_virtualwan_express_route_gateway` provisions the ExpressRoute gateway within a Virtual WAN hub, that ExpressRoute circuit connection(s) terminate on.
azure_network_virtualwan_hub_ip_configur: `azure_network_virtualwan_hub_ip_configuration` defines the IP configuration for a Virtual WAN hub's own routing infrastructure, e.g. for Azure Firewall integration.
azure_network_virtualwan_hub_route_table: `azure_network_virtualwan_hub_route_table` is a route table within a Virtual WAN hub controlling which routes are propagated to and associated with specific connection(s).
azure_network_virtualwan_hub_virtual_net: `azure_network_virtualwan_hub_virtual_network_connection` connects a spoke virtual network to a Virtual WAN hub, integrating it into the hub's own any-to-any routing topology.
azure_network_virtualwan_network_virtual: `azure_network_virtualwan_network_virtual_appliance_connection` connects a network virtual appliance deployed in a Virtual WAN hub to the hub's own routing infrastructure.
azure_network_virtualwan_p2_svpn_gateway: `azure_network_virtualwan_p2_svpn_gateway` provisions the point-to-site VPN gateway within a Virtual WAN hub, that individual remote client(s) connect to.
azure_network_virtualwan_route_map: `azure_network_virtualwan_route_map` transforms route attributes (prefix, community, AS-path) as they're advertised to or received from a Virtual WAN hub connection, for advanced routing policy scenarios.
azure_network_virtualwan_routing_intent: `azure_network_virtualwan_routing_intent` configures a Virtual WAN hub to route all internet-bound or private inter-hub traffic through a security appliance (e.g. Azure Firewall) by default, without manual route table configuration.
azure_network_virtualwan_virtual_hub: `azure_network_virtualwan_virtual_hub` is the regional routing hub within a Virtual WAN, that spoke virtual network(s), VPN/ExpressRoute gateway(s), and security appliance(s) connect to.
azure_network_virtualwan_virtual_hub_rou: `azure_network_virtualwan_virtual_hub_route_table_v2` is the current-generation route table resource for a Virtual WAN hub, supporting more granular route propagation and association rules than the original hub route table.
azure_network_virtualwan_virtual_wan: `azure_network_virtualwan_virtual_wan` is the top-level Virtual WAN resource that virtual hub(s) across regions are created within, providing a unified, Microsoft-managed global network backbone.
azure_network_virtualwan_vpn_connection: `azure_network_virtualwan_vpn_connection` connects a remote VPN site to a Virtual WAN hub's own site-to-site VPN gateway.
azure_network_virtualwan_vpn_gateway: `azure_network_virtualwan_vpn_gateway` provisions the site-to-site VPN gateway within a Virtual WAN hub, that VPN site connection(s) terminate on.
azure_network_virtualwan_vpn_gateway_nat: `azure_network_virtualwan_vpn_gateway_nat_rule` applies NAT translation to traffic passing through a Virtual WAN VPN gateway, for connecting sites with overlapping address spaces.
azure_network_virtualwan_vpn_server_conf: `azure_network_virtualwan_vpn_server_configuration` defines the authentication method and protocol(s) a Virtual WAN point-to-site VPN gateway accepts client connections with.

`azure_network_virtualwan_vpn_server_configuration_policy_group` groups point-to-site VPN client(s) by attribute (e.g. Entra ID group) and applies a distinct address pool or configuration to that group.
azure_network_virtualwan_vpn_site: `azure_network_virtualwan_vpn_site` represents a remote, on-premises site (its own address space and link details) that connects into a Virtual WAN hub via site-to-site VPN.
azure_newrelic_monitored_subscription_pr: `azure_newrelic_monitored_subscription_properties` adds an additional Azure subscription to be monitored by a New Relic resource, beyond the subscription it's deployed in.

azure_newrelic_tag_rule: `azure_newrelic_tag_rule` configures which resource tags include or exclude resource(s) from monitoring by a New Relic resource on Azure.
azure_nginx_swagger_nginx_certificate: `azure_nginx_swagger_nginx_certificate` uploads a TLS certificate (referenced from Key Vault) to an NGINX for Azure deployment.
azure_nginx_swagger_nginx_configuration_: `azure_nginx_swagger_nginx_configuration_response` is the current NGINX configuration file set applied to an NGINX for Azure deployment.
azure_nginx_swagger_nginx_deployment: `azure_nginx_swagger_nginx_deployment` is an NGINX for Azure (NGINXaaS) deployment, a fully managed NGINX Plus instance run and supported jointly by Microsoft and F5.
azure_nginx_swagger_nginx_deployment_api: `azure_nginx_swagger_nginx_deployment_api_key_response` is an API key issued for authenticating dataplane API calls to an NGINX for Azure deployment.
azure_nginx_swagger_nginx_deployment_waf: `azure_nginx_swagger_nginx_deployment_waf_policy` configures NGINX App Protect Web Application Firewall protection for an NGINX for Azure deployment.
azure_notificationhubs_namespace_resourc: `azure_notificationhubs_namespace_resource` is a Notification Hubs namespace, the management container that notification hub(s) are created within.

azure_notificationhubs_shared_access_aut: `azure_notificationhubs_shared_access_authorization_rule_resource` defines a shared access policy (with specific permissions) for connecting to a Notification Hubs namespace or hub.
azure_operationalinsights_openapi_cluste: `azure_operationalinsights_openapi_cluster` provisions a dedicated Log Analytics cluster, providing customer-managed key encryption and reserved ingestion capacity pricing across attached workspace(s).
azure_operationalinsights_openapi_data_e: `azure_operationalinsights_openapi_data_export` continuously exports matching Log Analytics workspace data (specific table(s)) to an external destination (a Storage account or Event Hub).

azure_operationalinsights_openapi_log_an: `azure_operationalinsights_openapi_log_analytics_query_pack` is a shareable collection of saved Log Analytics query/queries, reusable across multiple workspace(s) rather than saved to just one.

azure_operationalinsights_openapi_saved_: `azure_operationalinsights_openapi_saved_search` is a named, reusable Log Analytics query saved directly to a single workspace.
azure_operationalinsights_openapi_storag: `azure_operationalinsights_openapi_storage_insight` configures a Log Analytics workspace to ingest metrics and logs from an Azure Storage account.
azure_operationalinsights_openapi_summar: `azure_operationalinsights_openapi_summary_logs` schedules a Log Analytics query to run periodically and write its own aggregated results into a summary table, reducing the cost and latency of repeatedly re-running an expensive query.
azure_operationalinsights_openapi_table: `azure_operationalinsights_openapi_table` is a table within a Log Analytics workspace, holding ingested log data of a specific schema and its own retention/plan configuration.
azure_operationalinsights_openapi_worksp: `azure_operationalinsights_openapi_workspace` is a Log Analytics workspace, the top-level container log and telemetry data across Azure Monitor, Microsoft Sentinel, and other services is ingested into and queried from.

azure_oracle_openapi_virtual_network_add: `azure_oracle_openapi_virtual_network_address` reserves an IP address from an Azure virtual network's own address space for use by an Oracle Database@Azure resource.
